outcome: Use of neonatal respiratory support (positive pressure ventilation, continuous positive airway pressure, mechanical ventilator)
cohort: 94 extremely obese pregnant women (BMI >= 40.0 kg/m2) delivering at Seoul National University Bundang Hospital after late preterm gestation (excluding fetal death in utero and preterm births before 34 weeks of gestation).
finding: In extremely obese women delivering late preterm, those with lower pre-pregnancy BMI (but still obese) had higher rates of preterm labor with tocolytics and adverse neonatal respiratory outcomes compared to those already extremely obese, with increased weight gain during pregnancy further contributing to higher neonatal respiratory support use.
